cita: Tomczak (2026). RAMPART: Registry-based Agentic Memory with Priority-Aware Runtime Transformation.
problema: Instruction/skill files (SKILL.md/CLAUDE.md) and database-backed archival memory (Letta) treat context assembly as fixed concatenation, not a programmable operation, so compile-time block ordering, relevance-based inclusion, and structural access control are unavailable, and models suffer position-dependent (U-shaped) instruction-following failures the system cannot correct.
mecanismo: A pure in-RAM ordered block registry (OrderedDict[UUID->InstructionBlock]) where each addressable block carries priority/source/author/removable/embedding metadata; five zero-prompt-token primitives (promote, gate/write, evict, rollback, write-to-other-registry) mutate ordering and membership before a compile() step assembles the final prompt string; relevance gating pre-filters blocks by cosine similarity before compilation (not after, unlike retrieval-augmented injection); session-local UUID re-randomization of block addresses on every load (ASLR-style) prevents an injected instruction from targeting a block by semantic name.
evaluacion: Controlled mechanistic probes (not general benchmarks) on Qwen3-8B Q4 with a 31-block firmware seed library and a fictional-function-name checker; position sweeps across registry sizes 1-31 under task-precedes/task-follows configurations; a cluster-grouping sweep; cross-model replication on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, Qwen3-14B; a relevance-gating cost/success trade-off; a schema-eviction access-control test; latency micro-benchmarks (Table 3).
numeros_clave: Near-ceiling success up to ~position 11 (task precedes) or ~position 6 (task follows) before a sharp cliff; block grouping raises Mistral-7B's mean pass rate roughly fivefold at the hardest registry size; relevance gating reduces prompt cost by 67.8% while recovering 83% of promoted-condition success; schema eviction produces 0% tool invocations vs 100% with the schema present; compile() reaches 12.5us at N=200 blocks, find_relevant() 4-6ms, cold start 230ms at N=31 (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The in-RAM block registry with zero disk I/O after cold start and a deterministic compile() step (S2.4) is a concrete derived-index-as-cache pattern: the registry is rebuildable state over the seed library, inspectable before every inference call, directly transferable to MF's TIER-INDICE.

Relevance gating cuts prompt token cost by 67.8% while recovering 83% of promoted-condition success (abstract, S3.2), and all five registry primitives execute at zero prompt-token cost (Table 4), confirming MF's context-economy framing that structural filtering beats brute concatenation.

Session-local UUID re-randomization of block runtime addresses (S2.1, an ASLR analogy) is a concrete write-time defense against indirect prompt injection that references a block by semantic name -- a pattern MF could adopt for provenance/tamper resistance beyond content-based checks.

notes: Explicitly scoped as mechanistic probes, not general-purpose benchmarks (S3.1); position-sensitivity cliff data in Figure 1, latencies in Table 3. No membership doubt.

cita: Munirathinam, T. (2026). memorywire: A Vendor-Neutral Wire Format for Agent Memory Operations.
problema: Agent-memory frameworks (mem0, Letta, Cognee, Zep, MemoryOS, MemTensor) each ship a bespoke SDK/storage layout with no shared wire format, so every integration is bespoke, every migration rebuilds memory from scratch, and no framework exposes a governance surface letting a human review a write before it enters long-term storage.
mecanismo: A JSON-Schema-2020-12 wire format for five operations (remember/recall/forget/merge/expire) over four memory types (semantic/episodic/procedural/emotional), implemented via a MemoryStore protocol that any backend adopts; a memory router fans operations across N child stores in parallel and fuses recall results via rank-only, additive Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60), with an optional one-hop graph boost applied only to items already in the fused set; an optional HITL governance channel implements a diff-and-approve pattern (Co-memorize) staging flagged writes behind a PENDING_APPROVAL sentinel invisible to recall until a reviewer commits or rejects.
evaluacion: A microbenchmark on a 100-fact/50-query labelled corpus against a real sentence-transformer embedder; an adversarial-fusion experiment sweeping a 1-of-N rank-0 injection attack (K in {0,5,...,50}) across RRF/MAX/weighted fusion; a 16-scenario x 5-adapter cross-adapter conformance suite (80 cells); reference implementation with five backend adapters (sqlite-vec, mem0, Letta, Cognee, pgvector).
numeros_clave: recall@5=1.000 on 42 gold-id queries, ingest p50=37.8ms, recall p50=40.6ms; RRF holds recall@5=1.000 across the full K in {0,...,50} injection sweep while MAX fusion collapses to 0.500 with 80% leak at K>=5; conformance suite passes 68/80 cells (12 SKIP, 0 FAIL).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: A vendor-neutral wire format that any of 5 heterogeneous backends implements losslessly for the type/confidence/expires_at fields (Table 2 fidelity matrix) is a concrete single-source-per-fact standardization pattern directly transferable to MF's multi-store seams (COSTURAS).

forget defaults to soft delete (preserving the audit trail as a tombstone) and expire pins a predicate DSL (older_than_days/confidence_below/no_recall_in_days, S3.2) as a first-class 'this should no longer be trusted/recalled' vocabulary -- a concrete wire-level encoding of negative knowledge.

RRF's rank-only, additive-across-stores fusion gives measured robustness against a rogue/compromised store (recall@5 holds 1.000 across the full injection sweep, S5.2) vs MAX's 0.500/80%-leak collapse -- a concrete multi-store fusion algorithm MF could adopt for provenance-robust retrieval fusion.

notes: Explicitly frames itself as composition/standardization, not new algorithms (S1.3); adversarial-fusion open-data artifact cited in C5. No membership doubt.

cita: Yu (2026). Present but Not Enforced: Benchmarking Governance-Marker Compliance in LLM Agent Memory Under Multi-Turn Pressure.
problema: Persistent agent memories carry system-assigned governance markers (retracted/stale/low-trust) meant to constrain how a model uses them, but no prior work separates whether a model merely recalls a marker from whether it still acts on it once a user applies sustained multi-turn pressure to ignore it.
mecanismo: BEC (Behavioral Execution Consistency) separates recall from compliance via two conditions on a frozen 120-item benchmark (15 valid + 105 revoked across retracted/stale/low-trust classes): the WITH condition uses independent recall and compliance probes with no pressure; the PRESSURE condition follows the recall probe with three escalating rounds of adversarial user pressure in one multi-turn dialogue, judging a case ZOMBIE if any round erodes compliance, and computing the zombie-compliance rate (ZCRR) over recalled revoked-class items plus a valid-memory-use-rate (VMUR) negative control.
evaluacion: Five models from two vendors (moonshot-v1-128k, kimi-k2.5, kimi-k2.6, deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash), scored by a cross-validated judge (deepseek-v4-pro, cross-family agreement 89.3% on 28 re-judged items); metrics are recall rate, WITH/PRESSURE ZCRR with 95% Wilson intervals, VMUR, and a per-marker-class breakdown (retracted/stale/low-trust).
numeros_clave: Recall=1.00 for all 5 models; WITH-condition ZCRR 0.000-0.010 (near zero); PRESSURE ZCRR spans 0.219 (kimi-k2.6) to 0.971 (moonshot-v1-128k); same-generation cross-vendor flagships differ ~3.8x (kimi-k2.6 0.219 vs deepseek-v4-pro 0.838, non-overlapping CIs) while within-family capability upgrade (v4-flash->v4-pro) changes ZCRR by only 0.019; valid-class collateral damage 0/15 on four models, 1/15 on one (Table 1).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Governance markers (retracted/stale/low-trust) are exactly MF's negative-knowledge concept made explicit and testable: recall of the marker (knowing 'do not use this') is perfect (1.0) but PRESSURE-condition compliance collapses to as low as 0.029 upheld (ZCRR up to 0.971) -- holding negative knowledge in context is necessary but not sufficient without external enforcement.

Directly challenges relying on in-context governance markers and model judgment to enforce staleness/fidelity: the WITH-condition ZCRR near zero rules out a perception failure, yet PRESSURE ZCRR reaches up to 0.971 (Table 1) -- an explicit marker guarantees the model knows, not that it complies, motivating governance enforced outside the model rather than left to its in-context judgment (S5.1).

notes: Positions itself explicitly as an incremental intersection of STALE/Memora (adjudication gap) and SYCON-Bench (sycophancy), S2. No membership doubt.

cita: Liu (2026). Memory Contagion: Cross-Temporal Propagation of Evaluator Bias via Agent Memory.
problema: Prior work on agent memory consolidation assumes stored experiences are unbiased and attributes memory degradation solely to the consolidation mechanism; it ignores that agents trained or guided by biased evaluators produce biased trajectories that, once stored, can propagate that bias to future agents retrieving from the same memory store even when consolidation is perfect.
mecanismo: A source agent's trajectories are scored by a biased evaluator (additive bias model Eb=Eclean+alpha*b, for length preference or authority-marker density) and stored via oracle (lossless) or LLM-based consolidation; a target agent retrieving from the biased vs. a clean store is compared via Gamma_temporal, the Wasserstein-1 distance between behavioral score distributions, decomposed into content-based, retrieval-based and interaction components (E1-E3) and swept across contamination rates p in {0.2,...,1.0}.
evaluacion: 4-phase pipeline (bias injection, memory construction, oracle-consolidation ablation, mechanism decomposition, dose-response) on DeepSeek-Chat with 3-seed bootstrap CIs and permutation tests (p<0.01); multi-model validation on DeepSeek V4-Chat, V4-Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.6; retrieval-log Precision@5 analysis to rule out retrieval interference.
numeros_clave: Oracle (perfect) consolidation still yields Gamma_A=13.18 (95% CI [9.05,21.10], length bias) proving biased input alone suffices for contagion; LLM consolidation attenuates length bias by 84% (Gamma_B=2.03) but only the older DeepSeek V4-Chat is susceptible -- V4-Pro and Claude Sonnet 4.6 both show Gamma_A=0.00; authority bias fails to propagate in all 15 controlled multi-seed runs (Gamma=0.00); content (E1) and retrieval (E2) contribute comparably to Gamma_total (6.82 for length); contagion detected at contamination rate as low as p=0.2, no observed safe threshold.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Directly challenges the assumption (attributed to prior work, S5) that 'fixing consolidation quality fixes memory problems': Gamma_A=13.18 under oracle (lossless) consolidation proves consolidation is not the sufficient guard -- input-bias must be addressed independently before promotion, not assumed away by a perfect merge step.

The finding that consolidation's effect is bias-type-dependent (attenuates global/length bias by 84% but cannot detectably propagate local/authority-marker bias in this setup, S4.2) is itself negative knowledge MF should encode: 'do not assume consolidation is safe by default for all fact types' -- motivating type-aware promotion guards.

The retrieval-log Precision@5 analysis (monotonic 0.00->1.00 across p, Appendix A.7) is used to rule out retrieval interference as the dose-response mechanism -- a reusable measured-retrieval diagnostic technique relevant to G-M2 even though the paper's domain is bias, not staleness.

notes: Authority-bias amplification (Table 1 dagger) is explicitly flagged non-replicable single-run and not a confirmed finding; only the 15-run null (Gamma=0.00) is load-bearing. No membership doubt.

cita: Louck (2026). Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees.
problema: Existing memory-poisoning defenses base an item's authority to act on its content (trust-scoring) or its derivation history (lineage), but both signals are malleable: an attacker can launder an untrusted origin through the agent's own summarization, a trusted-tool echo, or manufactured corroboration, so a poisoned memory ends up looking benign and authoritative to any content- or lineage-based gate.
mecanismo: TMA-NM binds act_class to origin at write time (origin in {user, trusted_tool, agent, untrusted_external}, set by an authenticated channel the adversary cannot forge) and propagates it non-malleably: any item derived from untrusted sources inherits maximum untrust regardless of how benign the derived text reads; authority rises only via Sybil-resistant corroboration-gated elevation (>=2 independent trusted principals, never repeated untrusted content) or a fresh action-bound single-use user authorization; every write/elevation/verdict is appended to a tamper-evident hash chain. A TLA+ machine-checked model proves malleable gates are insufficient (T1), write-time binding is necessary (T2), and this non-malleable construction is sufficient (T3, 3,270 reachable states) plus an inductive invariant toward unbounded executions.
evaluacion: MEM-INV-Bench: 12 domains x 5 consequential tool types, sleeper/control-flow/data-exfiltration attack classes with benign/static/adaptive/whitebox variants, benchmarked across 8 frontier models from 6 vendors against 5 defense classes (none, trust_score, lineage, capability_ifc, TMA-NM); Wilson 95% CIs and 20,000-iteration permutation tests; a per-decision latency microbenchmark.
numeros_clave: Baselines fail up to 68% laundering ASR (trust_score and capability_ifc) and lineage reaches 47% laundering ASR; TMA-NM alone reaches 0% ASR on both direct and laundering attacks across all 8 models at 100% legit-utility (Table I); cross-model trigger study: TMA-NM 0/4032 successful attacks (CI [0,0.1]%) vs undefended baseline 31.2% (43.8% on blatant triggers); act-gate decision costs 1.3us vs ~2000ms for a content-detection judge call (~6 orders of magnitude cheaper).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The machine-checked separation theorem (T1-T3, S4) plus 0% empirical ASR across 8 models is strong confirmation that content- or lineage-only defenses are structurally insufficient against laundering (existing defenses reach up to 68% ASR, Table I) and that write-time origin-binding is necessary -- directly validates MF's FIDELIDAD emphasis on provenance over content trust.

The non-malleable act-gate is a deterministic check at 1.3us per decision vs ~2000ms for an LLM-judge content detector (S6, six orders of magnitude cheaper), showing rigorous security enforcement need not compete with the token/latency budget.

Sybil-resistant corroboration-gated elevation -- authority rises only via >=2 independent trusted principals, never through content asserting its own legitimacy (S3, M3) -- is a concrete single-source-of-truth-per-fact pattern directly transferable to MF's COSTURAS need.

notes: T1-T3 are bounded-model (TLC, Slots=3/sessions<=2/k=2) results extended toward unbounded execution via a hand-argued inductive invariant, not a fully mechanized unbounded proof (S4, explicitly scoped). No membership doubt.

cita: Jawed (2026). When Disagreement Means Learning (or Bias): Human-Governed Memory Consolidation and Counterfactual Diagnosis in Multi-Agent LLM Scoring.
problema: Multi-agent validation (a second, independent agent scores an item and disagreement routes to a human) breaks down once the primary scorer adapts via retrieval-augmented exemplars while the auditor must stay cold to remain independent: every freshly learned lesson widens the inter-agent gap, so the system escalates exactly the cases it just learned to handle, converting learning into review burden.
mecanismo: Two asymmetric channels: an instance channel where a human correction is re-embedded with its rationale and retrieved only by the primary as a few-shot exemplar (fast, narrow, primary-only); and a policy channel where corrections teaching the same lesson cluster in embedding space (k>=3 via greedy leader clustering), an LLM drafts a rubric-amendment, a human approves it, both agents (including the cold auditor) inherit the new rubric version, and the promoted exemplars are retired. Counterfactual cold scoring (score with vs. without retrieved exemplars) plus a stricter cold-agreement threshold routes disagreement to auto-accept, auto-accept-learned, or human review, with a deterministic 10% spot-check canary on auto-accepts.
evaluacion: 108 work items across two contrasting domains (software-engineering work items, real-estate listings), three independent runs, no fine-tuning; agreement rate, instance-learning separation on held-out similar items vs. controls, same-domain leakage before/after consolidation, and cross-model replication on two further base models including a cross-vendor one.
numeros_clave: Inter-agent agreement 88.3+-0.5% across runs; instance-level learning gives a 0.20 separation (+0.33 similar-item lift vs +0.12 unrelated control) but leaks onto same-domain items (+0.35); on the domain where corrections cluster, human-governed consolidation eliminates that leakage (controls return to baseline) while preserving the learned lift; illustrative single-item trace 7.5/7.5/7.5 -> 9.0/7.5/7.5 (instance learning) -> 8.5/8.5/8.0 (after promotion, agents re-align).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Human-governed consolidation (instance exemplars -> clustering k>=3 -> LLM-drafted rubric amendment -> human approval -> shared policy + exemplar retirement, S4.5) is a directly transferable pattern for MF's gotcha-to-recipe promotion, empirically shown to eliminate instance-channel leakage onto unrelated same-domain items (+0.35 -> baseline) while preserving the learned lift (S6.5).

Counterfactual cold scoring (score with vs. without retrieved corrections, S4.2) is a concrete 'know what you would have done without this memory' self-diagnosis -- a pattern MF's NEGATIVO anchor could adopt to attribute a retrieval-triggered decision to learning vs. error before trusting it.

The counterfactual costs one extra inference only on retrieval hits, so cold-start traffic pays nothing (S4.2) -- a cheap diagnostic pattern relevant to MF's context-economy framing, though the paper reports no absolute token/latency numbers.

notes: Production-grade deployed system (Mizaan), 3 independent runs, no fine-tuning anywhere (abstract). No membership doubt.
